DURBAN BOMB THREATS

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A spate of bomb scares are terrorizing the people of Durban - are we dealing with terror attacks? Extortion? Or just simply very dangerous attention seeking?

Unique Selling Point:
- topical
- not being addressed properly by authorities
- panic and paranoia spreading

Summary:
Panic spreads through Durban as 10 bomb scares in three weeks in public shopping areas raise questions that police can’t seem to answer – who is behind it and what could they hope to achieve?

The main theory for the motive behind the placing of incendiary devices in Durban seems to lean to wards Extortion rather than terrorism - Pay up or face the fire.

But with targets getting bigger – are we dealing with a potential lonewolf with dangerous intentions as he becomes increasingly infamous.


Further information:
WHAT WE KNOW
• There have been 10 incidents in KZN, half were hoaxes, the other half were real explosive devices.
• TARGETS: SPAR, multiple WOOLIES, three shopping centres and a police station.
• Only one incident of asking for money – the rest no one has claimed the act or demanded anything.

WHAT WE KNOW THAT HASN’T BEEN REPORTED
• The devices are made by the same person
• It can’t be a vendetta against Woolies – other places also targeted.
• The same type of device was found at the Veralum Mosque Bomb threat
• These devices at this stage will not blow up a building – might take off a hand or result in minor injuries
• The person responsible appears to be enjoying the fame, but is growing braver with bigger targets – last week Thursday a high rise building in the CBD was evacuated.

WHAT THE SECURITY EXPERTS SAY
WILLEM ELS – INSTITUTE SECURITY STUDIES – EXPERT IN TERRORISM, EX-BOMB SQUAD.

Els, an expert in crime scene handling and bomb disposal at the Institute for Security Studies, believes that if terrorists had been responsible, they would claim credit for such acts and ride on the media hype. “This has not happened,” he said.

Els said the type of targets had to be considered. While pipe bombs were detonated near cars parked in Greyville at the Vodacom Durban July, incendiary devices had been found at Woolworths, Spar and “apparently some small businesses”. This “definitely points towards this direction that it might be extortion”, said Els. Els stressed that his thoughts about extortion remained speculation, adding that very little information was available.
“There is not a lot of sharing of information from the police. They are scared it could jeopardise investigations. People want to be reassured that police are on top of it,” Els said.
“With ‘bombs’, there is always panic, fear and insecurity. If the public are not reassured, there will be that hype,” added Els. He noted that it appeared this tactic of placing incendiary devices appeared to be restricted to Durban.

WHAT THE POLICE SAY
SAPS spokesman Vish Naidoo said police resources were being "exhausted" on hoax calls relating to suspicious parcels.

"These hoax calls are draining police resources. We have to respond to every call and we have found that 60 to 65% of these are hoax calls‚ particularly during school holidays."

In the past two weeks several incendiary devices were planted at other Woolworths stores in the city as well as at the Vodacom Durban July. These devices‚ rudimentary in nature‚ have been triggered and caused minor fires.

CRITICISM FOR COPS
they are accused of not handling it appropriately - not informing the public of the investigation or allaying fears.

WOOLWORTHS
The store chain will be beefing up security. This as the retailer has become the target of bomb threats over suspicious devices found either in its aisles or storerooms. The source is yet to be identified.

As recently as Thursday, the police bomb disposal unit was called in to search a Woolworths shop in the Durban city centre for evidence of another "bomb" after a staff member at the shop found a suspicious device. Two other shops, in the Gateway and Pavillion shopping malls, have been victims of similar incidents over the past two weeks.

Kay Raidoo, Woolworths head of divisions, said that "following the recent security incidents in and around Durban, particularly within three of our stores, I want to offer you my assurance that your safety and the safety of our people remains our primary concern".
"At this stage the motive behind these incidents is unclear and the investigation is ongoing. We continue to work closely with the relevant authorities, including the South African Police Service, the Hawks' crimes against [the] state unit, local and national government, as well as our own investigators who are providing input and guidance," Naidoo said in a statement.

"You will, however, now notice that additional uniformed security guards have been placed in all our KZN stores. We have also instituted a new search process which is for your safety and protection." Naidoo said Woolworths realised that the extra security measures may cause some inconvenience as all shops were open for trading, but "we are trying our best to minimise any disruption to your shopping experience".

INCIDENTS
MAY 2018
Verulam mosque – same kind of device

05 July 2018
- WOOLWORTHS GATEWAY SHOPPING CENTRE
- WOOLWORTHS PAVILION SHOPPING CENTRE

07 July 2018
- NEAR GREYVILLE RACE COURSE – VODACOM JULY 2018 – AVONDALE ROAD
- WOOLWORTHS GATEWAY SHOPPING CENTRE - The device, hidden among cushions, was found to be a cellphone attached to a short length of white PVC pipe.

09 July 2018
- PAVILION Shopping Centre - The device was allegedly found in an underground parking lot - the device was found not to have been an explosive, but rather a discarded security tag.
- Spar in Austerville in Wentworth – boy 10, bomb found

12 July 2018
- the Phoenix police station had to be evacuated following a bomb threat hoax.
- the Cornubia Mall in Mount Edgecombe was evacuated for the same reason - no device was found at the Woolworths store or anywhere else at the shopping mall. The police did a full security sweep and nothing suspicious was found - https://www.iol.co.za/dailynews/phoenix-police-station-and-cornubia-bomb-scare-a-hoax-15976402

19 July 2018
- WOOLWORTHS, DBN CBD - Pine Street
- A garage and Woolworths convenience store in Ilala Ridge‚ Umhlanga - Just after 10am, reports circulated that employees were evacuated from the Woolworths store, just off uMhlanga Rocks Drive, after a suspicious device was found lying on the floor. Police and members of the SAPS Bomb unit were deployed to the scene. However, it turned out that the "device" was a firecracker -used at events.

18 July 2018
- The Wynberg Boys’ Junior School has been on lockdown after a “potential security threat” was received of a bomb inside the premises.

14 July 2018
- On Saturday, shoppers were also forced to evacuate Kenilworth Shopping Centre after a person was warned about an explosive device in one of the stores.

- WILLEM ELS – ISS
- SPAR
- WOOLIES
- SAPS – VISH NAIDOO
- SA COUNCIL FOR SHOPPING CENTRES

Press Release:


It’s the biggest mystery currently facing officials in Durban – ten explosive devices have been found in a number of popular shopping malls around the city. While half of the bomb scares in Durban seem to have been hoaxes, in some cases, specialist police were called in to safely detonate the dangerous combustible devices. Residents are terrified and it seems Crime Intelligence have run out of answers. With two more explosive devices also recovered in Cape Town, Carte Blanche investigates what’s really behind this the spate of bomb scares

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: It may not look like it, but the laidback east coast city of Durban in KwaZulu Natal is on edge (under threat). There have been at least 11 bomb threats in just three weeks across the city, at various public locations.

VOX POPS:
VP4 M1: It’s been a little bit uneasy
VP7 M1: I’m very, very scared to be honest with you it’s very scary
VP2 M2: I do feel very afraid, because i dont know if it is real, if it’s not real

LINK: // The targets have varied, there’s no specific area and the motives have yet to be determined – are we talking terrorism, extortion or a dark kind of attention seeking?

WILLEM: // There is a pattern in the attacks. You can also see that it is calculated // I think it is an orchestrated campaign that is going on. INT1 M4

LINK: The first incident was here at the Pavilion Shopping Centre in Westville – an explosive device detonated in men’s clothing section of Woolworths. Shoppers were evacuated. The bomb squad arrived and managed to // contain it inside the store. But this was just the beginning.

VO: On the same day, a similar device detonated at the Gateway Shopping Centre also in the men’s clothing section of Woolworths. [5 July 2018]

Then, just two days later, the same Woolworths store was hit again. This time, the device was successfully defused without detonation by the bomb squad. It was found hidden amongst cushions on the shop floor – you can see here that the device had a cellphone attached to a short length of white PVC pipe.

LINK: This is an example of one the devices that was found in the shopping centres – and the reality is that if you look at what it takes to makes it –you could buy most of it in a hardware store – but the truth of the matter is that is this is not childsplay – this is criminality. PIPE BOMB

VISH: It is a serious crime – you can be charged in terms of the explosives acts and if found guilty you will go to jail – there is no option of a fine. // INT1 M19

VO: SAPS spokesperson, Brigadier Vish Naidoo insists that these devices were not designed to cause major damage.

VISH: The devices that we are finding are not explosives and they are not bombs – these are incendiary devices that has a potential to perhaps start a fire. – it doesn’t have the potential to cause an explosion or massive destruction.. INT1 M1

VO: While explosives expert, Willem Els agrees that the damage caused by these devices would be minimal – they are still bombs.

WILLEM: you don’t have a guarantee on how it was constructed and how well it was constructed – you don’t have a guarantee that it will just burn. INT1 M10 // // we must be cautious not to downplay it to such an extent that people are not worried about it. INT1 M12

VO: The reality is that while homemade devices may appear rudimentary, they are unpredictable and should not be underestimated.

WILLEM: I think we are looking at more professional bomb builders – indications are that it is not just a fly by night that got up one morning and decided they are going to build a bomb. INT1 M14 // the level of expertise when it comes to the triggering devices – in order to alter that cellphone you need a certain level of skills INT1 M13

VO: The next target? Two separate devices were planted and exploded under cars parked close to the Greyville Racecourse, where the Vodacom Durban July was underway. [7 July 2018]

Two days later, things took a sinister turn with the next threat.

LINK: Here at the Spar in Wentworth it was the first time that a demand was linked to a bomb threat – could this be another player jumping in on the action - opening the door to extortion. A boy was sent to the supermarket to hand the manager a brown envelope containing a 9mm bullet and a handwritten letter demanding cash in a bag or a bomb would explode.

VO: The bomb squad safely detonated the device.

While this incident appears to have been an opportunistic copy cat, there has also been a string of hoax calls adding to the chaos.

CHRISTIAAN: We // refer to that as a possibility of the contagion effect –

VO: Criminologist Professor Christiaan Bezuidenhout explains there is usually a surge in hoax calls after bomb threats.

CHRISTIAAN: // people start copy catting – they copy cat what other people are doing for the media attention – recognition in the media, and they get a sort of thrill, a satisfaction out of this. INT1 M9

VO: There was a false alarm at the Pavilion Shopping Centre [9 July 2018] and two hoaxes where no devices were found – one at the Phoenix Police Station [12 July 2018] and one at Cornubia Mall [12 July 2018] in Mount Edgecombe. [sit datums op screen]

Pippa Botha is a personal trainer at Cornubia.

PIPPA: We didn’t think it was real until one of the staff came through and siad we’re evacuating, it’s and actual threat. INT1 M2

VO: Staff and shoppers gathered at assembly points, while the police swept the mall.

PIPPA: People were generally chilled // It wasn’t crazy it was basically, i have to say, it was pretty chilled.
DEVI: were you scared?
PIPPA: obviously there is that air of a threat, but i wasn’t.

VO: Pippa is not alone in her chilled approach - some Durbanites were completely oblivious to the incidents, while others weren’t phased at all.

VOX POPS:
VP: I haven’t seen it (black guy)
VP: INDIAN GUY
VP8 M1: ….would have been more drastic….

VO: Trends indicate that people only tend to react once there has been serious devastation or a loss of life, according to Professor Bezuidenhout.

CHRISTIAAN: // I think the south African community = the society has become blaze – we have normalised crime – we have been battered with murder, rape, robbery, hijacking /INT1 M1

VO: But as Durbanites remain seemingly unphased, the threats continue.

The next legitimate incident was in the CBD. A suspicious device was found inside this Woolworths – roads were cordoned off and surrounding shops were evacuated while police neutralised the device. [19 July 2018]

MARTIN: it is really, really escalating // INT1 M8// / Downplaying it could also be very dangerous because you never know when these devices are armed and could cause serious problem. INT1 M11

VO: International Terrorism Expert Martin Ewi is from the Institute for Security Studies.

MARTIN: // we’ve seen terrorists use the kinds of devices that we have seen used in South Africa recently // INT1 M4 // it is something extremely dangerous – we have seen in other regions the havoc this kind of weapon has created. // INT1 M1/

VO: Although no one has claimed responsibility for the incidents - Ewi says terrorism should not be ruled out as a motive. Terrorism is very simply the use of indiscriminate violence to create fear among masses of people.

It’s important to note, that international terror attacks are not always claimed immediately.

CHRISTIAAN: Even in your global terrorists issues you get situations where people do not claim responsibility but they start off slow to see, to infiltrate, infiltrate and see – and then they strike. INT 1 M26

VO: The police are exploring all motives at this stage according to Brigadier Naidoo.

VISH: we are in a process of conducting a modus operandi analysis on this whole thing – it Is difficult from our assessments so far, to say there is potential of it escalating or de-escalating – what has happened – it seems that their MO is constant. INT1 M18

VO: Explosives expert Willem Els believes in addition to the modus operandi, the actual devices should have a wealth of information.

WILLEM: When you discover these devices there will be traces and with very good and thorough investigation they will get the leads and it will lead to arrests of the people – eventually. INT1 M20

VO: The affected retailers say they are cooperating with the police and have implemented additional security measures in KZN.

DEVI: Have there been any arrests?
VISH: No arrests yet - an investigation of this nature is not just a run of the mill investigation – it’s a very sensitive investigation, // there are various factors that may influence something like this // INT1 M12

VO: But Ewi believes the police can do more to keep the public informed of developments.

MARTIN: I know that the police do a lot of work behind the scenes - the only problem I have had with the approach that they have used is the lack of communication with the population // INT1 M12 // The government has been concerned about creating panic // INT1 M13

VO: In the meantime, South Africans should be alert and vigilant.

CHRISTIAAN: // do not underestimate the power and the reason why people use these initiatives. INT1 M21


PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: A number of explosive devices found in Durban in just THREE weeks. Is it Terrorism? Extortion? Or attention seeking?

WILLEM: // There is a pattern in the attacks. You can also see that it is calculated // INT1 M4

PROMO 2
VO: Three weeks of bomb threats across the city of Durban – with no arrests yet – what are the motives - an act of terrorism or pranksters at work?

WILLEM: I think we are looking at more professional bomb builders – indications are that it is not just a fly by night that got up one morning and decided they are going to build a bomb. INT1 M14


PROMO 3
VO: Bomb threats across Durban have gripped the city - but these devices are not toys and the penalties are serious.

VISH: You can be charged in terms of the explosives acts and if found guilty you will go to jail – there is no option of a fine. // INT1 M19


PROMO 4
VO: Three weeks of bomb threats across the city of Durban – with no arrests yet – what are the motives – extortion, terrorism or pranksters at work?

WILLEM: // There is a pattern in the attacks. You can also see that it is calculated // I think we are looking at more professional bomb builders INT1 M14

VO: These devices are not toys and the penalties are serious.

VISH: You can be charged in terms of the explosives acts and if found guilty you will go to jail. // INT1 M19

VOX POPS: VP4 M1: It’s been a little bit uneasy VP7 M1: I’m very, very scared to be honest with you it’s very scary VP2 M2: I do feel very afraid, because i dont know if it is real, if it’s not real LINK: // The targets have varied, there’s no specific area and the motives have yet to be determined – are we talking terrorism, extortion or a dark kind of attention seeking? WILLEM: // There is a pattern in the attacks. You can also see that it is calculated // I think it is an orchestrated campaign that is going on. INT1 M4 LINK: The first incident was here at the Pavilion Shopping Centre in Westville – an explosive device detonated in men’s clothing section of Woolworths. Shoppers were evacuated. The bomb squad arrived and managed to // contain it inside the store. But this was just the beginning. VO: On the same day, a similar device detonated at the Gateway Shopping Centre also in the men’s clothing section of Woolworths. [5 July 2018] Then, just two days later, the same Woolworths store was hit again. This time, the device was successfully defused without detonation by the bomb squad. It was found hidden amongst cushions on the shop floor – you can see here that the device had a cellphone attached to a short length of white PVC pipe. LINK: This is an example of one the devices that was found in the shopping centres – and the reality is that if you look at what it takes to makes it –you could buy most of it in a hardware store – but the truth of the matter is that is this is not childsplay – this is criminality. PIPE BOMB VISH: It is a serious crime – you can be charged in terms of the explosives acts and if found guilty you will go to jail – there is no option of a fine. // INT1 M19 VO: SAPS spokesperson, Brigadier Vish Naidoo insists that these devices were not designed to cause major damage. VISH: The devices that we are finding are not explosives and they are not bombs – these are incendiary devices that has a potential to perhaps start a fire. – it doesn’t have the potential to cause an explosion or massive destruction.. INT1 M1 VO: While explosives expert, Willem Els agrees that the damage caused by these devices would be minimal – they are still bombs. WILLEM: you don’t have a guarantee on how it was constructed and how well it was constructed – you don’t have a guarantee that it will just burn. INT1 M10 // // we must be cautious not to downplay it to such an extent that people are not worried about it. INT1 M12 VO: The reality is that while homemade devices may appear rudimentary, they are unpredictable and should not be underestimated. WILLEM: I think we are looking at more professional bomb builders – indications are that it is not just a fly by night that got up one morning and decided they are going to build a bomb. INT1 M14 // the level of expertise when it comes to the triggering devices – in order to alter that cellphone you need a certain level of skills INT1 M13 VO: The next target? Two separate devices were planted and exploded under cars parked close to the Greyville Racecourse, where the Vodacom Durban July was underway. [7 July 2018] Two days later, things took a sinister turn with the next threat. LINK: Here at the Spar in Wentworth it was the first time that a demand was linked to a bomb threat – could this be another player jumping in on the action - opening the door to extortion. A boy was sent to the supermarket to hand the manager a brown envelope containing a 9mm bullet and a handwritten letter demanding cash in a bag or a bomb would explode. VO: The bomb squad safely detonated the device. While this incident appears to have been an opportunistic copy cat, there has also been a string of hoax calls adding to the chaos. CHRISTIAAN: We // refer to that as a possibility of the contagion effect – VO: Criminologist Professor Christiaan Bezuidenhout explains there is usually a surge in hoax calls after bomb threats. CHRISTIAAN: // people start copy catting – they copy cat what other people are doing for the media attention – recognition in the media, and they get a sort of thrill, a satisfaction out of this. INT1 M9 VO: There was a false alarm at the Pavilion Shopping Centre [9 July 2018] and two hoaxes where no devices were found – one at the Phoenix Police Station [12 July 2018] and one at Cornubia Mall [12 July 2018] in Mount Edgecombe. [sit datums op screen] Pippa Botha is a personal trainer at Cornubia. PIPPA: We didn’t think it was real until one of the staff came through and siad we’re evacuating, it’s and actual threat. INT1 M2 VO: Staff and shoppers gathered at assembly points, while the police swept the mall. PIPPA: People were generally chilled // It wasn’t crazy it was basically, i have to say, it was pretty chilled. DEVI: were you scared? PIPPA: obviously there is that air of a threat, but i wasn’t. VO: Pippa is not alone in her chilled approach - some Durbanites were completely oblivious to the incidents, while others weren’t phased at all. VOX POPS: VP: I haven’t seen it (black guy) VP: INDIAN GUY VP8 M1: ….would have been more drastic…. VO: Trends indicate that people only tend to react once there has been serious devastation or a loss of life, according to Professor Bezuidenhout. CHRISTIAAN: // I think the south African community = the society has become blaze – we have normalised crime – we have been battered with murder, rape, robbery, hijacking /INT1 M1 VO: But as Durbanites remain seemingly unphased, the threats continue. The next legitimate incident was in the CBD. A suspicious device was found inside this Woolworths – roads were cordoned off and surrounding shops were evacuated while police neutralised the device. [19 July 2018] MARTIN: it is really, really escalating // INT1 M8// / Downplaying it could also be very dangerous because you never know when these devices are armed and could cause serious problem. INT1 M11 VO: International Terrorism Expert Martin Ewi is from the Institute for Security Studies. MARTIN: // we’ve seen terrorists use the kinds of devices that we have seen used in South Africa recently // INT1 M4 // it is something extremely dangerous – we have seen in other regions the havoc this kind of weapon has created. // INT1 M1/ VO: Although no one has claimed responsibility for the incidents - Ewi says terrorism should not be ruled out as a motive. Terrorism is very simply the use of indiscriminate violence to create fear among masses of people. It’s important to note, that international terror attacks are not always claimed immediately. CHRISTIAAN: Even in your global terrorists issues you get situations where people do not claim responsibility but they start off slow to see, to infiltrate, infiltrate and see – and then they strike. INT 1 M26 VO: The police are exploring all motives at this stage according to Brigadier Naidoo. VISH: we are in a process of conducting a modus operandi analysis on this whole thing – it Is difficult from our assessments so far, to say there is potential of it escalating or de-escalating – what has happened – it seems that their MO is constant. INT1 M18 VO: Explosives expert Willem Els believes in addition to the modus operandi, the actual devices should have a wealth of information. WILLEM: When you discover these devices there will be traces and with very good and thorough investigation they will get the leads and it will lead to arrests of the people – eventually. INT1 M20 VO: The affected retailers say they are cooperating with the police and have implemented additional security measures in KZN. DEVI: Have there been any arrests? VISH: No arrests yet - an investigation of this nature is not just a run of the mill investigation – it’s a very sensitive investigation, // there are various factors that may influence something like this // INT1 M12 VO: But Ewi believes the police can do more to keep the public informed of developments. MARTIN: I know that the police do a lot of work behind the scenes - the only problem I have had with the approach that they have used is the lack of communication with the population // INT1 M12 // The government has been concerned about creating panic // INT1 M13 VO: In the meantime, South Africans should be alert and vigilant. CHRISTIAAN: // do not underestimate the power and the reason why people use these initiatives. INT1 M21 PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: A number of explosive devices found in Durban in just THREE weeks. Is it Terrorism? Extortion? Or attention seeking? WILLEM: // There is a pattern in the attacks. You can also see that it is calculated // INT1 M4 PROMO 2 VO: Three weeks of bomb threats across the city of Durban – with no arrests yet – what are the motives - an act of terrorism or pranksters at work? WILLEM: I think we are looking at more professional bomb builders – indications are that it is not just a fly by night that got up one morning and decided they are going to build a bomb. INT1 M14 PROMO 3 VO: Bomb threats across Durban have gripped the city - but these devices are not toys and the penalties are serious. You can also see that it is calculated // I think we are looking at more professional bomb builders INT1 M14 VO: These devices are not toys and the penalties are serious. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A spate of bomb scares are terrorizing the people of Durban - are we dealing with terror attacks? Extortion? Or just simply very dangerous attention seeking?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: - topical - not being addressed properly by authorities - panic and paranoia spreading
metadata.Summary: Panic spreads through Durban as 10 bomb scares in three weeks in public shopping areas raise questions that police can’t seem to answer – who is behind it and what could they hope to achieve? The main theory for the motive behind the placing of incendiary devices in Durban seems to lean to wards Extortion rather than terrorism - Pay up or face the fire. But with targets getting bigger – are we dealing with a potential lonewolf with dangerous intentions as he becomes increasingly infamous.
metadata.Further information: WHAT WE KNOW • There have been 10 incidents in KZN, half were hoaxes, the other half were real explosive devices. • TARGETS: SPAR, multiple WOOLIES, three shopping centres and a police station. • Only one incident of asking for money – the rest no one has claimed the act or demanded anything. WHAT WE KNOW THAT HASN’T BEEN REPORTED • The devices are made by the same person • It can’t be a vendetta against Woolies – other places also targeted. • The same type of device was found at the Veralum Mosque Bomb threat • These devices at this stage will not blow up a building – might take off a hand or result in minor injuries • The person responsible appears to be enjoying the fame, but is growing braver with bigger targets – last week Thursday a high rise building in the CBD was evacuated. WHAT THE SECURITY EXPERTS SAY WILLEM ELS – INSTITUTE SECURITY STUDIES – EXPERT IN TERRORISM, EX-BOMB SQUAD. Els, an expert in crime scene handling and bomb disposal at the Institute for Security Studies, believes that if terrorists had been responsible, they would claim credit for such acts and ride on the media hype. “This has not happened,” he said. Els said the type of targets had to be considered. While pipe bombs were detonated near cars parked in Greyville at the Vodacom Durban July, incendiary devices had been found at Woolworths, Spar and “apparently some small businesses”. This “definitely points towards this direction that it might be extortion”, said Els. Els stressed that his thoughts about extortion remained speculation, adding that very little information was available. “There is not a lot of sharing of information from the police. They are scared it could jeopardise investigations. People want to be reassured that police are on top of it,” Els said. “With ‘bombs’, there is always panic, fear and insecurity. If the public are not reassured, there will be that hype,” added Els. He noted that it appeared this tactic of placing incendiary devices appeared to be restricted to Durban. WHAT THE POLICE SAY SAPS spokesman Vish Naidoo said police resources were being "exhausted" on hoax calls relating to suspicious parcels. "These hoax calls are draining police resources. We have to respond to every call and we have found that 60 to 65% of these are hoax calls‚ particularly during school holidays." In the past two weeks several incendiary devices were planted at other Woolworths stores in the city as well as at the Vodacom Durban July. These devices‚ rudimentary in nature‚ have been triggered and caused minor fires. CRITICISM FOR COPS they are accused of not handling it appropriately - not informing the public of the investigation or allaying fears. WOOLWORTHS The store chain will be beefing up security. This as the retailer has become the target of bomb threats over suspicious devices found either in its aisles or storerooms. The source is yet to be identified. As recently as Thursday, the police bomb disposal unit was called in to search a Woolworths shop in the Durban city centre for evidence of another "bomb" after a staff member at the shop found a suspicious device. Two other shops, in the Gateway and Pavillion shopping malls, have been victims of similar incidents over the past two weeks. Kay Raidoo, Woolworths head of divisions, said that "following the recent security incidents in and around Durban, particularly within three of our stores, I want to offer you my assurance that your safety and the safety of our people remains our primary concern". "At this stage the motive behind these incidents is unclear and the investigation is ongoing. We continue to work closely with the relevant authorities, including the South African Police Service, the Hawks' crimes against [the] state unit, local and national government, as well as our own investigators who are providing input and guidance," Naidoo said in a statement. "You will, however, now notice that additional uniformed security guards have been placed in all our KZN stores. We have also instituted a new search process which is for your safety and protection." Naidoo said Woolworths realised that the extra security measures may cause some inconvenience as all shops were open for trading, but "we are trying our best to minimise any disruption to your shopping experience". INCIDENTS MAY 2018 Verulam mosque – same kind of device 05 July 2018 - WOOLWORTHS GATEWAY SHOPPING CENTRE - WOOLWORTHS PAVILION SHOPPING CENTRE 07 July 2018 - NEAR GREYVILLE RACE COURSE – VODACOM JULY 2018 – AVONDALE ROAD - WOOLWORTHS GATEWAY SHOPPING CENTRE - The device, hidden among cushions, was found to be a cellphone attached to a short length of white PVC pipe. 09 July 2018 - PAVILION Shopping Centre - The device was allegedly found in an underground parking lot - the device was found not to have been an explosive, but rather a discarded security tag. - Spar in Austerville in Wentworth – boy 10, bomb found 12 July 2018 - the Phoenix police station had to be evacuated following a bomb threat hoax. - the Cornubia Mall in Mount Edgecombe was evacuated for the same reason - no device was found at the Woolworths store or anywhere else at the shopping mall. The police did a full security sweep and nothing suspicious was found - https://www.iol.co.za/dailynews/phoenix-police-station-and-cornubia-bomb-scare-a-hoax-15976402 19 July 2018 - WOOLWORTHS, DBN CBD - Pine Street - A garage and Woolworths convenience store in Ilala Ridge‚ Umhlanga - Just after 10am, reports circulated that employees were evacuated from the Woolworths store, just off uMhlanga Rocks Drive, after a suspicious device was found lying on the floor. Police and members of the SAPS Bomb unit were deployed to the scene. However, it turned out that the "device" was a firecracker -used at events. CPT 18 July 2018 - The Wynberg Boys’ Junior School has been on lockdown after a “potential security threat” was received of a bomb inside the premises. 14 July 2018 - On Saturday, shoppers were also forced to evacuate Kenilworth Shopping Centre after a person was warned about an explosive device in one of the stores.
